"""Steps 5 and 6: evaluate the trained classifiers on the held-out test years (malware = positive class)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, confusion_matrix, f1_score, precision_score, recall_score

from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS
from src.data import write_data_summary

METRIC_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = ("accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1")


def compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Accuracy, precision, recall and F1 with malware (label 1) as the positive class."""
    kwargs = {"pos_label": 1, "zero_division": 0}  # zero_division=0: no predicted/actual malware gives 0, not an error
    return {
        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
        "precision": float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
        "recall": float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
        "f1": float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
    }


def confusion_counts(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Confusion matrix as TN, FP, FN, TP counts (labels fixed to [0, 1] so a missing class still gives 2x2)."""
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    return {"tn": int(tn), "fp": int(fp), "fn": int(fn), "tp": int(tp)}


def assert_test_years_only(years: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError if any year is outside TEST_YEARS (metrics must never be computed on training years)."""
    bad = sorted(set(np.unique(years).tolist()) - set(TEST_YEARS))
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"evaluation data contains years outside {TEST_YEARS}: {bad}")


def _check_same_length(X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError if X_test and y_test have different numbers of rows."""
    if len(X_test) != len(y_test):
        raise ValueError(f"X_test has {len(X_test)} rows but y_test has {len(y_test)}")


def evaluate_model(model: Any, X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Predict with a fitted model and return its four metrics."""
    return compute_metrics(y_test, model.predict(X_test))


def pooled_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per classifier: model, accuracy, precision, recall, f1, n_test (pooled over the test years)."""
    _check_same_length(X_test, y_test)
    rows = [{"model": name, **evaluate_model(m, X_test, y_test), "n_test": len(y_test)} for name, m in models.items()]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", *METRIC_NAMES, "n_test"])


def per_year_table(
    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per (model, test year): metrics plus year and n."""
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    rows = []
    for name, m in models.items():
        pred = m.predict(X_test)  # predict once, slice per year
        for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
            sel = years_test == year
            rows.append({"model": name, "year": int(year), **compute_metrics(y_test[sel], pred[sel]), "n": int(sel.sum())})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "year", *METRIC_NAMES, "n"])


def drift_summary(per_year: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per model: F1 in the first and last test year, the drop between them, and the least-squares F1 slope per year."""
    rows = []
    for name, g in per_year.groupby("model", sort=False):
        g = g.sort_values("year")
        first, last = float(g["f1"].iloc[0]), float(g["f1"].iloc[-1])
        slope = float(np.polyfit(g["year"].to_numpy(dtype=float), g["f1"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 1)[0]) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0
        rows.append({"model": name, "first_year": int(g["year"].iloc[0]), "last_year": int(g["year"].iloc[-1]),
                     "f1_first": first, "f1_last": last, "f1_drop": first - last, "f1_slope_per_year": slope})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def year_baseline_table(y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per test year: n, malware/benign counts, malware share and majority-class (baseline) accuracy."""
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    rows = []
    for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
        y = y_test[years_test == year]
        rows.append({"year": int(year), "n": len(y), "n_malware": int((y == 1).sum()), "n_benign": int((y == 0).sum()),
                     "malware_share": float(np.mean(y == 1)), "baseline_accuracy": baseline_accuracy(y)})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def by_year_export(per_year: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Step 6 file layout: columns classifier, year, n, accuracy, precision, recall, f1."""
    out = per_year.rename(columns={"model": "classifier"})
    return out[["classifier", "year", "n", *METRIC_NAMES]]


def plot_by_year(per_year: pd.DataFrame, path: Path) -> None:
    """Save a two-panel figure (F1 and accuracy by test year, one line per classifier) to path."""
    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")  # no display needed
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4), sharex=True)
    for ax, metric in zip(axes, ("f1", "accuracy")):
        for name, g in per_year.groupby("model", sort=False):
            g = g.sort_values("year")
            ax.plot(g["year"], g[metric], marker="o", label=name)
        ax.set_title(f"{metric.upper() if metric == 'f1' else metric.capitalize()} by test year")
        ax.set_xlabel("test year")
        ax.set_xticks(sorted(per_year["year"].unique()))
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("score (malware = positive class)")
    axes[0].legend()
    fig.tight_layout()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=120)
    plt.close(fig)


def confusion_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per classifier with pooled tn, fp, fn, tp counts."""
    _check_same_length(X_test, y_test)
    return pd.DataFrame([{"model": n, **confusion_counts(y_test, m.predict(X_test))} for n, m in models.items()])


def baseline_accuracy(y_test: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Accuracy of always predicting the majority class of y_test."""
    return float(max(np.mean(y_test == 1), np.mean(y_test == 0)))


def sensitivity_tables(
    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray, dup_mask: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Pooled and per-year tables on test rows with NO exact duplicate in the training years (dup_mask False).

    Each table gets an n_excluded column (rows removed by the filter; per year for the per-year table).
    The pooled table also gets n_malware/n_benign (kept) and n_excluded_malware/n_excluded_benign, so the
    change in class mix caused by the filter is visible.
    """
    dup_mask = np.asarray(dup_mask, dtype=bool)
    if len(dup_mask) != len(y_test):
        raise ValueError(f"dup_mask has {len(dup_mask)} entries but there are {len(y_test)} test rows")
    keep = ~dup_mask
    if keep.sum() == 0:
        raise ValueError("every test row has an exact duplicate in the training years; nothing left to evaluate")
    pooled = pooled_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep])
    pooled["n_excluded"] = int(dup_mask.sum())
    # Class counts kept and removed (label 1 = malware, 0 = benign).
    pooled["n_malware"] = int((y_test[keep] == 1).sum())
    pooled["n_benign"] = int((y_test[keep] == 0).sum())
    pooled["n_excluded_malware"] = int((y_test[dup_mask] == 1).sum())
    pooled["n_excluded_benign"] = int((y_test[dup_mask] == 0).sum())
    per_year = per_year_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep], years_test[keep])
    excluded = pd.Series(years_test[dup_mask]).value_counts()
    per_year["n_excluded"] = per_year["year"].map(lambda y: int(excluded.get(y, 0)))
    return pooled, per_year


def save_table(df: pd.DataFrame, stem: str) -> None:
    """Write results/<stem>.csv and results/<stem>.md (floats rounded to 4 decimals in both)."""
    write_data_summary(df.round(4), RESULTS_DIR / stem)

"""Step 3: year split, log1p, feature filters and scaling (fit on training years only)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Iterable

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from src.config import (
    LABEL_COL,
    MIN_SUPPORT,
    TEST_YEARS,
    TRAIN_YEARS,
    TUNE_TRAIN_YEARS,
    TUNE_VAL_YEAR,
    YEAR_COL,
    Z_CLIP,
)
from src.data import feature_columns


def check_no_overlap(train_years: Iterable[int], test_years: Iterable[int]) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError unless train and test years are non-empty, disjoint, and every train year precedes every test year."""
    train, test = set(train_years), set(test_years)
    if not train or not test:
        raise ValueError("train_years and test_years must both be non-empty")
    if train & test:
        raise ValueError(f"train and test years overlap: {sorted(train & test)}")
    if max(train) >= min(test):
        raise ValueError(f"training years {sorted(train)} must all precede test years {sorted(test)}")


def split_by_year(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    train_years: Iterable[int] = TRAIN_YEARS,
    test_years: Iterable[int] = TEST_YEARS,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return (train, test) frames selected by the `year` column, after checking the years cannot leak."""
    train_years, test_years = tuple(train_years), tuple(test_years)
    check_no_overlap(train_years, test_years)  # guard first: nothing is selected for a bad split
    train = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(train_years)]
    test = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(test_years)]
    # Every requested year must be present, otherwise the split is silently smaller than asked for.
    for name, part, years in (("train", train, train_years), ("test", test, test_years)):
        missing = sorted(set(years) - set(part[YEAR_COL].unique()))
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"requested {name} years missing from the data: {missing}")
    return train, test


def apply_log1p(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return log(1 + X) as float32; raises ValueError on NaN/inf or negative input (counts must be finite and >= 0)."""
    if not np.isfinite(X).all():  # checked once here, so fit and transform each pay for it once per call
        raise ValueError("log1p input must be finite (no NaN or inf)")
    if X.size and X.min() < 0:
        raise ValueError("log1p input must be non-negative")
    return np.log1p(X, dtype=np.float32)


def nonzero_feature_mask(X_train: np.ndarray, min_support: int = MIN_SUPPORT) -> np.ndarray:
    """Boolean mask of columns with at least `min_support` non-zero values in the TRAINING rows."""
    if min_support < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"min_support must be >= 1, got {min_support}")
    return (X_train != 0).sum(axis=0) >= min_support


class Preprocessor:
    """log1p -> minimum-support column filter -> StandardScaler -> fixed clip, all learned from training rows only.

    sklearn-like (fit/transform/fit_transform), not a BaseEstimator: no get_params, not usable in a Pipeline.
    """

    def __init__(self, min_support: int = MIN_SUPPORT) -> None:
        """Store the support threshold; nothing is learned until `fit`."""
        if min_support < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"min_support must be >= 1, got {min_support}")
        self.min_support = min_support
        self.scaler: StandardScaler | None = None
        self.mask_: np.ndarray | None = None
        self.feature_names_in_: list[str] | None = None
        self.kept_features_: list[str] | None = None
        self.n_all_zero_: int = 0

    def fit(self, X_train_raw: np.ndarray, feature_names: list[str] | None = None) -> "Preprocessor":
        """Learn the column mask and the scaler from raw training counts."""
        X = apply_log1p(X_train_raw)  # log1p keeps zeros at zero, so the mask is the same on raw or logged data
        self.mask_ = nonzero_feature_mask(X, self.min_support)
        self.n_all_zero_ = int((~(X != 0).any(axis=0)).sum())
        names = feature_names if feature_names is not None else [str(i) for i in range(X.shape[1])]
        if len(names) != X.shape[1]:
            raise ValueError(f"got {len(names)} feature names for {X.shape[1]} columns")
        self.feature_names_in_ = list(names)
        self.kept_features_ = [n for n, keep in zip(names, self.mask_) if keep]
        self.scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X[:, self.mask_])
        return self

    def transform(self, X_raw: np.ndarray, clip: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
        """Apply the fitted log1p, mask and scaler (never refits), clip to +-Z_CLIP; returns float32.

        `clip=False` is only for reporting the size of the extreme values.
        """
        if self.scaler is None or self.mask_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Preprocessor must be fit before transform")
        if X_raw.shape[1] != len(self.mask_):
            raise ValueError(f"expected {len(self.mask_)} columns (as in fit), got {X_raw.shape[1]}")
        X = apply_log1p(X_raw)[:, self.mask_]
        Z = self.scaler.transform(X).astype(np.float32)
        # Fixed constant clip: the same for train and test, nothing learned from any data.
        return np.clip(Z, -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP, out=Z) if clip else Z

    def fit_transform(self, X_train_raw: np.ndarray, feature_names: list[str] | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
        """Fit on the training counts and return them transformed."""
        return self.fit(X_train_raw, feature_names).transform(X_train_raw)


def _split_arrays(train: pd.DataFrame, test: pd.DataFrame, features: list[str]) -> dict:
    """Pull raw feature matrices, labels and years out of the train/test frames."""
    return {
        "X_train_raw": train[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32),
        "y_train": train[LABEL_COL].to_numpy(),
        "years_train": train[YEAR_COL].to_numpy(),
        "X_test_raw": test[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32),
        "y_test": test[LABEL_COL].to_numpy(),
        "years_test": test[YEAR_COL].to_numpy(),
    }


def prepare_split(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    train_years: Iterable[int] = TRAIN_YEARS,
    test_years: Iterable[int] = TEST_YEARS,
) -> dict:
    """Split by year, fit a Preprocessor on the training rows only, transform both sides with it."""
    features = feature_columns(df)
    train, test = split_by_year(df, train_years, test_years)
    a = _split_arrays(train, test, features)
    X_train_raw, X_test_raw = a.pop("X_train_raw"), a.pop("X_test_raw")
    pre = Preprocessor().fit(X_train_raw, features)  # training rows only
    X_train, X_test = pre.transform(X_train_raw, clip=False), pre.transform(X_test_raw, clip=False)
    clip_stats = clip_report(X_train, X_test)  # measured before clipping
    np.clip(X_train, -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP, out=X_train)
    np.clip(X_test, -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP, out=X_test)
    return {"X_train": X_train, "X_test": X_test, "preprocessor": pre, "clip_stats": clip_stats, **a}


def clip_report(X_train: np.ndarray, X_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Max abs z and number of entries beyond +-Z_CLIP for UNCLIPPED scaled matrices; also the values after clipping."""
    rows = []
    for side, X in (("train", X_train), ("test", X_test)):
        A = np.abs(X)
        rows.append((side, float(A.max()), int((A > Z_CLIP).sum()), float(min(A.max(), Z_CLIP)), 0))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["side", "max_abs_z_before", "n_clipped", "max_abs_z_after", "n_beyond_clip_after"])


def make_tuning_split(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Same as `prepare_split`, but train on 2014-2015 and validate on 2016 (for tuning only)."""
    return prepare_split(df, TUNE_TRAIN_YEARS, (TUNE_VAL_YEAR,))


def filter_report(df: pd.DataFrame, pre: Preprocessor, test_years: Iterable[int]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Feature counts after each filter, plus columns active in the test years but dropped by the training-only mask."""
    features = feature_columns(df)
    test = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(tuple(test_years))]
    test_active = (test[features].to_numpy() != 0).any(axis=0)
    n_total = len(features)
    n_nonzero = n_total - pre.n_all_zero_
    n_kept = int(pre.mask_.sum())
    rows = [
        ("raw features", n_total),
        ("after dropping all-zero training columns", n_nonzero),
        (f"after min support >= {pre.min_support} training rows", n_kept),
        ("dropped for low support (1 to min_support-1 non-zero rows)", n_nonzero - n_kept),
        ("dropped columns that are non-zero somewhere in the test years", int((test_active & ~pre.mask_).sum())),
    ]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["stage", "n_features"])


def split_table(split: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rows and class balance per year on each side of the split."""
    rows = []
    for side in ("train", "test"):
        years, y = split[f"years_{side}"], split[f"y_{side}"]
        for year in sorted(set(years)):
            m = years == year
            rows.append((side, int(year), int(m.sum()), int(y[m].sum()), int((1 - y[m]).sum())))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["side", "year", "rows", "malware", "benign"])

101	    """
102	    df = load_all() if df is None else df
103	    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
104	    if models is None:

106	    X_test, y_test, years_test = split["X_test"], split["y_test"], split["years_test"]
107	    assert_test_years_only(years_test)

109	    base = baseline_accuracy(y_test)
110	    main_table["baseline_accuracy"] = base  # majority-class reference for the accuracy column
111	    # Mask over all rows of df; select the test rows (split_by_year keeps df order).
112	    dup_mask = train_duplicate_mask(df)[df["year"].isin(TEST_YEARS).to_numpy()]
113	    no_dup, _ = sensitivity_tables(models, X_test, y_test, years_test, dup_mask)

1	"""Steps 5 and 6: evaluate the trained classifiers on the held-out test years (malware = positive class)."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from pathlib import Path
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	import numpy as np
8	import pandas as pd
9	from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, confusion_matrix, f1_score, precision_score, recall_score
10	
11	from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS
12	from src.data import write_data_summary
13	
14	METRIC_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = ("accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1")

17	def compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
18	    """Accuracy, precision, recall and F1 with malware (label 1) as the positive class."""
19	    kwargs = {"pos_label": 1, "zero_division": 0}  # zero_division=0: no predicted/actual malware gives 0, not an error
20	    return {
21	        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
22	        "precision": float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
23	        "recall": float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
24	        "f1": float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
25	    }
26	
27	
28	def confusion_counts(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, int]:
29	    """Confusion matrix as TN, FP, FN, TP counts (labels fixed to [0, 1] so a missing class still gives 2x2)."""
30	    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
31	    return {"tn": int(tn), "fp": int(fp), "fn": int(fn), "tp": int(tp)}

34	def assert_test_years_only(years: np.ndarray) -> None:
35	    """Raise ValueError if any year is outside TEST_YEARS (metrics must never be computed on training years)."""
36	    bad = sorted(set(np.unique(years).tolist()) - set(TEST_YEARS))
37	    if bad:
38	        raise ValueError(f"evaluation data contains years outside {TEST_YEARS}: {bad}")
39

41	def _check_same_length(X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> None:
42	    """Raise ValueError if X_test and y_test have different numbers of rows."""
43	    if len(X_test) != len(y_test):
44	        raise ValueError(f"X_test has {len(X_test)} rows but y_test has {len(y_test)}")
45	
46	
47	def evaluate_model(model: Any, X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
48	    """Predict with a fitted model and return its four metrics."""
49	    return compute_metrics(y_test, model.predict(X_test))
50	
51	
52	def pooled_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
53	    """One row per classifier: model, accuracy, precision, recall, f1, n_test (pooled over the test years)."""
54	    _check_same_length(X_test, y_test)
55	    rows = [{"model": name, **evaluate_model(m, X_test, y_test), "n_test": len(y_test)} for name, m in models.items()]
56	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", *METRIC_NAMES, "n_test"])
57	
58	
59	def per_year_table(
60	    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray
61	) -> pd.DataFrame:
62	    """One row per (model, test year): metrics plus year and n."""
63	    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
64	    rows = []
65	    for name, m in models.items():
66	        pred = m.predict(X_test)  # predict once, slice per year
67	        for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
68	            sel = years_test == year
69	            rows.append({"model": name, "year": int(year), **compute_metrics(y_test[sel], pred[sel]), "n": int(sel.sum())})
70	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "year", *METRIC_NAMES, "n"])
71

73	def drift_summary(per_year: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
74	    """Per model: F1 in the first and last test year, the drop between them, and the least-squares F1 slope per year."""
75	    rows = []
76	    for name, g in per_year.groupby("model", sort=False):
77	        g = g.sort_values("year")
78	        first, last = float(g["f1"].iloc[0]), float(g["f1"].iloc[-1])
79	        slope = float(np.polyfit(g["year"].to_numpy(dtype=float), g["f1"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 1)[0]) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0
80	        rows.append({"model": name, "first_year": int(g["year"].iloc[0]), "last_year": int(g["year"].iloc[-1]),
81	                     "f1_first": first, "f1_last": last, "f1_drop": first - last, "f1_slope_per_year": slope})
82	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
83

85	def year_baseline_table(y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
86	    """Per test year: n, malware/benign counts, malware share and majority-class (baseline) accuracy."""
87	    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
88	    rows = []
89	    for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
90	        y = y_test[years_test == year]
91	        rows.append({"year": int(year), "n": len(y), "n_malware": int((y == 1).sum()), "n_benign": int((y == 0).sum()),
92	                     "malware_share": float(np.mean(y == 1)), "baseline_accuracy": baseline_accuracy(y)})
93	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

98	    out = per_year.rename(columns={"model": "classifier"})
99	    return out[["classifier", "year", "n", *METRIC_NAMES]]

126	def confusion_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
127	    """One row per classifier with pooled tn, fp, fn, tp counts."""
128	    _check_same_length(X_test, y_test)
129	    return pd.DataFrame([{"model": n, **confusion_counts(y_test, m.predict(X_test))} for n, m in models.items()])

132	def baseline_accuracy(y_test: np.ndarray) -> float:
133	    """Accuracy of always predicting the majority class of y_test."""
134	    return float(max(np.mean(y_test == 1), np.mean(y_test == 0)))

137	def sensitivity_tables(
138	    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray, dup_mask: np.ndarray
139	) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
140	    """Pooled and per-year tables on test rows with NO exact duplicate in the training years (dup_mask False).
141	
142	    Each table gets an n_excluded column (rows removed by the filter; per year for the per-year table).
143	    The pooled table also gets n_malware/n_benign (kept) and n_excluded_malware/n_excluded_benign, so the
144	    change in class mix caused by the filter is visible.
145	    """
146	    dup_mask = np.asarray(dup_mask, dtype=bool)
147	    if len(dup_mask) != len(y_test):
148	        raise ValueError(f"dup_mask has {len(dup_mask)} entries but there are {len(y_test)} test rows")
149	    keep = ~dup_mask
150	    if keep.sum() == 0:
151	        raise ValueError("every test row has an exact duplicate in the training years; nothing left to evaluate")
152	    pooled = pooled_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep])
153	    pooled["n_excluded"] = int(dup_mask.sum())
154	    # Class counts kept and removed (label 1 = malware, 0 = benign).
155	    pooled["n_malware"] = int((y_test[keep] == 1).sum())
156	    pooled["n_benign"] = int((y_test[keep] == 0).sum())
157	    pooled["n_excluded_malware"] = int((y_test[dup_mask] == 1).sum())
158	    pooled["n_excluded_benign"] = int((y_test[dup_mask] == 0).sum())
159	    per_year = per_year_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep], years_test[keep])
160	    excluded = pd.Series(years_test[dup_mask]).value_counts()
161	    per_year["n_excluded"] = per_year["year"].map(lambda y: int(excluded.get(y, 0)))
162	    return pooled, per_year
163

167	    write_data_summary(df.round(4), RESULTS_DIR / stem)

1	"""Step 3: year split, log1p, feature filters and scaling (fit on training years only)."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	from typing import Iterable
5	
6	import numpy as np
7	import pandas as pd
8	from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
9	
10	from src.config import (
11	    LABEL_COL,
12	    MIN_SUPPORT,
13	    TEST_YEARS,
14	    TRAIN_YEARS,
15	    TUNE_TRAIN_YEARS,
16	    TUNE_VAL_YEAR,
17	    YEAR_COL,
18	    Z_CLIP,
19	)
20	from src.data import feature_columns
21	
22	
23	def check_no_overlap(train_years: Iterable[int], test_years: Iterable[int]) -> None:
24	    """Raise ValueError unless train and test years are non-empty, disjoint, and every train year precedes every test year."""
25	    train, test = set(train_years), set(test_years)
26	    if not train or not test:
27	        raise ValueError("train_years and test_years must both be non-empty")
28	    if train & test:
29	        raise ValueError(f"train and test years overlap: {sorted(train & test)}")
30	    if max(train) >= min(test):
31	        raise ValueError(f"training years {sorted(train)} must all precede test years {sorted(test)}")
32	
33	
34	def split_by_year(
35	    df: pd.DataFrame,
36	    train_years: Iterable[int] = TRAIN_YEARS,
37	    test_years: Iterable[int] = TEST_YEARS,
38	) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
39	    """Return (train, test) frames selected by the `year` column, after checking the years cannot leak."""
40	    train_years, test_years = tuple(train_years), tuple(test_years)
41	    check_no_overlap(train_years, test_years)  # guard first: nothing is selected for a bad split
42	    train = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(train_years)]
43	    test = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(test_years)]
44	    # Every requested year must be present, otherwise the split is silently smaller than asked for.
45	    for name, part, years in (("train", train, train_years), ("test", test, test_years)):
46	        missing = sorted(set(years) - set(part[YEAR_COL].unique()))
47	        if missing:
48	            raise ValueError(f"requested {name} years missing from the data: {missing}")
49	    return train, test
50	
51	
52	def apply_log1p(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
53	    """Return log(1 + X) as float32; raises ValueError on NaN/inf or negative input (counts must be finite and >= 0)."""
54	    if not np.isfinite(X).all():  # checked once here, so fit and transform each pay for it once per call
55	        raise ValueError("log1p input must be finite (no NaN or inf)")
56	    if X.size and X.min() < 0:
57	        raise ValueError("log1p input must be non-negative")
58	    return np.log1p(X, dtype=np.float32)
59	
60	
61	def nonzero_feature_mask(X_train: np.ndarray, min_support: int = MIN_SUPPORT) -> np.ndarray:
62	    """Boolean mask of columns with at least `min_support` non-zero values in the TRAINING rows."""
63	    if min_support < 1:
64	        raise ValueError(f"min_support must be >= 1, got {min_support}")
65	    return (X_train != 0).sum(axis=0) >= min_support
66	
67	
68	class Preprocessor:
69	    """log1p -> minimum-support column filter -> StandardScaler -> fixed clip, all learned from training rows only.
70	
71	    sklearn-like (fit/transform/fit_transform), not a BaseEstimator: no get_params, not usable in a Pipeline.
72	    """
73	
74	    def __init__(self, min_support: int = MIN_SUPPORT) -> None:
75	        """Store the support threshold; nothing is learned until `fit`."""
76	        if min_support < 1:
77	            raise ValueError(f"min_support must be >= 1, got {min_support}")
78	        self.min_support = min_support
79	        self.scaler: StandardScaler | None = None
80	        self.mask_: np.ndarray | None = None
81	        self.feature_names_in_: list[str] | None = None
82	        self.kept_features_: list[str] | None = None
83	        self.n_all_zero_: int = 0
84	
85	    def fit(self, X_train_raw: np.ndarray, feature_names: list[str] | None = None) -> "Preprocessor":
86	        """Learn the column mask and the scaler from raw training counts."""
87	        X = apply_log1p(X_train_raw)  # log1p keeps zeros at zero, so the mask is the same on raw or logged data
88	        self.mask_ = nonzero_feature_mask(X, self.min_support)
89	        self.n_all_zero_ = int((~(X != 0).any(axis=0)).sum())
90	        names = feature_names if feature_names is not None else [str(i) for i in range(X.shape[1])]
91	        if len(names) != X.shape[1]:
92	            raise ValueError(f"got {len(names)} feature names for {X.shape[1]} columns")
93	        self.feature_names_in_ = list(names)
94	        self.kept_features_ = [n for n, keep in zip(names, self.mask_) if keep]
95	        self.scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X[:, self.mask_])
96	        return self
97	
98	    def transform(self, X_raw: np.ndarray, clip: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
99	        """Apply the fitted log1p, mask and scaler (never refits), clip to +-Z_CLIP; returns float32.
100	
101	        `clip=False` is only for reporting the size of the extreme values.
102	        """
103	        if self.scaler is None or self.mask_ is None:
104	            raise RuntimeError("Preprocessor must be fit before transform")
105	        if X_raw.shape[1] != len(self.mask_):
106	            raise ValueError(f"expected {len(self.mask_)} columns (as in fit), got {X_raw.shape[1]}")
107	        X = apply_log1p(X_raw)[:, self.mask_]
108	        Z = self.scaler.transform(X).astype(np.float32)
109	        # Fixed constant clip: the same for train and test, nothing learned from any data.
110	        return np.clip(Z, -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP, out=Z) if clip else Z
111	
112	    def fit_transform(self, X_train_raw: np.ndarray, feature_names: list[str] | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
113	        """Fit on the training counts and return them transformed."""
114	        return self.fit(X_train_raw, feature_names).transform(X_train_raw)
115	
116	
117	def _split_arrays(train: pd.DataFrame, test: pd.DataFrame, features: list[str]) -> dict:
118	    """Pull raw feature matrices, labels and years out of the train/test frames."""
119	    return {
120	        "X_train_raw": train[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32),
121	        "y_train": train[LABEL_COL].to_numpy(),
122	        "years_train": train[YEAR_COL].to_numpy(),
123	        "X_test_raw": test[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32),
124	        "y_test": test[LABEL_COL].to_numpy(),
125	        "years_test": test[YEAR_COL].to_numpy(),
126	    }
127	
128	
129	def prepare_split(
130	    df: pd.DataFrame,
131	    train_years: Iterable[int] = TRAIN_YEARS,
132	    test_years: Iterable[int] = TEST_YEARS,
133	) -> dict:
134	    """Split by year, fit a Preprocessor on the training rows only, transform both sides with it."""
135	    features = feature_columns(df)
136	    train, test = split_by_year(df, train_years, test_years)
137	    a = _split_arrays(train, test, features)
138	    X_train_raw, X_test_raw = a.pop("X_train_raw"), a.pop("X_test_raw")
139	    pre = Preprocessor().fit(X_train_raw, features)  # training rows only
140	    X_train, X_test = pre.transform(X_train_raw, clip=False), pre.transform(X_test_raw, clip=False)
141	    clip_stats = clip_report(X_train, X_test)  # measured before clipping
142	    np.clip(X_train, -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP, out=X_train)
143	    np.clip(X_test, -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP, out=X_test)
144	    return {"X_train": X_train, "X_test": X_test, "preprocessor": pre, "clip_stats": clip_stats, **a}
145	
146	
147	def clip_report(X_train: np.ndarray, X_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
148	    """Max abs z and number of entries beyond +-Z_CLIP for UNCLIPPED scaled matrices; also the values after clipping."""
149	    rows = []
150	    for side, X in (("train", X_train), ("test", X_test)):
151	        A = np.abs(X)
152	        rows.append((side, float(A.max()), int((A > Z_CLIP).sum()), float(min(A.max(), Z_CLIP)), 0))
153	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["side", "max_abs_z_before", "n_clipped", "max_abs_z_after", "n_beyond_clip_after"])
154	
155	
156	def make_tuning_split(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
157	    """Same as `prepare_split`, but train on 2014-2015 and validate on 2016 (for tuning only)."""
158	    return prepare_split(df, TUNE_TRAIN_YEARS, (TUNE_VAL_YEAR,))
159	
160	
161	def filter_report(df: pd.DataFrame, pre: Preprocessor, test_years: Iterable[int]) -> pd.DataFrame:
162	    """Feature counts after each filter, plus columns active in the test years but dropped by the training-only mask."""
163	    features = feature_columns(df)
164	    test = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(tuple(test_years))]
165	    test_active = (test[features].to_numpy() != 0).any(axis=0)
166	    n_total = len(features)
167	    n_nonzero = n_total - pre.n_all_zero_
168	    n_kept = int(pre.mask_.sum())
169	    rows = [
170	        ("raw features", n_total),
171	        ("after dropping all-zero training columns", n_nonzero),
172	        (f"after min support >= {pre.min_support} training rows", n_kept),
173	        ("dropped for low support (1 to min_support-1 non-zero rows)", n_nonzero - n_kept),
174	        ("dropped columns that are non-zero somewhere in the test years", int((test_active & ~pre.mask_).sum())),
175	    ]
176	    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["stage", "n_features"])

179	def split_table(split: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
180	    """Rows and class balance per year on each side of the split."""
181	    rows = []
182	    for side in ("train", "test"):
183	        years, y = split[f"years_{side}"], split[f"y_{side}"]
184	        for year in sorted(set(years)):
185	            m = years == year
186	            rows.append((side, int(year), int(m.sum()), int(y[m].sum()), int((1 - y[m]).sum())))

5	## What was done
6	
7	- Each trained classifier (logreg, random forest, SGD; fit on 2014-2016 only in Step 4) predicts each test year 2017-2021 separately. The models and the preprocessor are not refit or tuned on any test year; test rows only go through `transform` and `predict`. `assert_test_years_only` raises if any other year is passed.

9	- Malware (label 1) is the positive class. Every test year is exactly 50% malware and 50% goodware (table below), so the majority-class baseline accuracy is 0.5000 in every year.
10	- Files: `results/step6_by_year.csv|md` (columns `classifier, year, n, accuracy, precision, recall, f1`), `results/step6_baseline_by_year.csv|md`, `results/step6_drift_summary.csv|md`, `results/step6_per_year_no_dup.csv|md`, `results/step6_by_year.png`.

41	
42	![F1 and accuracy by test year](../results/step6_by_year.png)
43	
44	## Effect of drift
45	
46	**Shape of the decline.** Performance does not fall gradually with distance from the 2014-2016 training period. For 2017 and 2018 all three classifiers are strong (accuracy 0.91-0.96, F1 0.90-0.96, 41-46 points above the 0.5 baseline). From 2017 to 2018 the change is small: F1 drops 0.0166 (logreg) and 0.0171 (random forest) and rises 0.0139 for SGD. Then from 2018 to 2019 there is a cliff: F1 drops by 0.2552 (logreg), 0.2534 (random forest) and 0.2410 (SGD). Accuracy in 2019-2021 is 0.504-0.549, i.e. 0.4 to 4.9 points above the majority-class baseline of 0.5000. After 2019 there is no consistent further decline: F1 for 2019, 2020 and 2021 is within 0.018 for each classifier (logreg 0.012, random forest 0.017, SGD 0.010).
47	
48	**What the models do in 2019-2021.** Recall stays very high (0.980-1.000) while precision falls to 0.502-0.526. This is the pattern of a classifier that labels almost everything as malware. For example, for logreg in 2021, precision 0.5063 with recall 0.9920 (1,488 of 1,500 malware caught) implies about 1,451 of the 1,500 goodware apps flagged (derived from the two numbers, about 97%). An F1 of about 0.667 is exactly the F1 of a model that always predicts malware on a balanced set (2*0.5/(0.5+1)); the 2019-2021 F1 values (0.6668-0.6875) are only 0.0001-0.0208 above that. So the F1 of 0.67 should not be read as "moderate" performance: accuracy shows these years are close to chance. The classes are balanced in every year, so the low precision comes from many false positives, not from the class mix.
49	
50	**Per-year drift summary** (`results/step6_drift_summary.csv`, first test year 2017 vs last 2021):
51	
52	| Classifier | F1 2017 | F1 2021 | F1 drop | F1 slope per year |
53	|---|---|---|---|---|
54	| logreg | 0.9514 | 0.6704 | 0.2810 | -0.0829 |
55	| random_forest | 0.9580 | 0.6701 | 0.2879 | -0.0845 |
56	| sgd | 0.9039 | 0.6695 | 0.2344 | -0.0720 |
57	
58	The slope is a straight-line fit over five points whose pattern is a step, so it describes the size of the drop but not its shape. SGD has the smallest drop only because it starts lowest in 2017.
59	
60	**Classifier comparison.** The random forest has the highest F1 in 2017, 2018 and 2019 and logreg is close behind (0.006-0.007 lower in 2017-2018). SGD is lowest in 2017 and 2018 (F1 0.9039 and 0.9178; 0.048-0.054 below the others in 2017, 0.017-0.023 in 2018). In 2020 and 2021 the three classifiers are within 0.005 (2020) and 0.001 (2021) F1 of each other. None of the three is robust to the change at 2019, and no classifier ranking in 2019-2021 is reliable (see noise below).
61	
62	## Comparison with the Step 2 drift numbers
63	
64	Step 2 mean KS statistic vs 2014 (`results/step2_ks_vs_2014.csv`, each year balanced to 3,000 rows):
65	
66	| Year | 2015 | 2016 | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 |
67	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
68	| mean KS vs 2014 | 0.0226 | 0.0363 | 0.0437 | 0.0432 | 0.0515 | 0.0612 | 0.0849 |
69	| share significant | 0.164 | 0.218 | 0.259 | 0.251 | 0.273 | 0.347 | 0.369 |
70	
71	**Do the years with the most drift have the lowest F1? Partly.** The three years with the largest KS vs 2014 (2021, 2020, 2019) are the three years with the lowest F1 and accuracy for every classifier, and the two lowest-KS test years (2018 and 2017, 0.0432 and 0.0437) have the highest F1. The direction agrees. But the size does not match: mean KS rises only from 0.0437 (2017) to 0.0515 (2019), while F1 falls by about 0.27. Within 2019-2021, KS keeps rising (0.0515, 0.0612, 0.0849) while F1 and accuracy stay flat near chance, and F1 is not ordered by KS (for logreg, 2020 is slightly lower than 2021; for random forest, 2021 is slightly lower than 2020). 2017 has a slightly higher KS than 2018 (0.0437 vs 0.0432, a gap of 0.0005) but a higher F1 for logreg and random forest; I do not read anything into so small a KS gap. The consecutive-year KS (`results/step2_ks_consecutive.csv`) has no spike at the 2018 to 2019 step: 2018-2019 is 0.0277, close to 2016-2017 (0.0276) and 2019-2020 (0.0231), and the largest consecutive value is 2020-2021 (0.0487), where F1 does not change. So the mean KS statistic does not locate the cliff.
72	
73	The Step 2 accuracy matrix (`results/step2_accuracy_matrix.csv`, 3,000 balanced rows per year, a logistic regression fit on a single year) does show the same cliff. The model trained on 2016 scores 0.9667 on 2017 and 0.9353 on 2018, then 0.5743, 0.5410 and 0.3507 on 2019, 2020 and 2021. Models trained on 2014, 2015, 2017 and 2018 also score only 0.52-0.67 on 2019-2021, so the cliff is not caused by the 2014-2016 training period being old: models trained on 2017 or 2018 fail on 2019-2021 as well. By contrast the models trained on 2019, 2020 and 2021 do well on each other (0.73-0.94) and worse on earlier years (0.57-0.85). This suggests that the 2019-2021 data differ from 2014-2018 in a way that a model fit on 2014-2018 does not transfer (the relationship between features and label, not only the feature distribution, which is concept drift in the Step 2 sense). I did not test why. Possible reasons that I have not checked: a real change in malware and goodware behaviour, or a different collection or labelling process for the smaller 2019-2021 files (they also have 3,000 rows against 18,000, and far fewer repeated apknames, Step 1).
74	
75	## Sensitivity: test rows with no exact duplicate in 2014-2016
76	
77	Files: `results/step6_per_year_no_dup.csv|md`. Rows whose exact feature vector also occurs in 2014-2016 are removed (5,972 of 18,000 in 2017, 1,645 in 2018, 57 in 2019, 67 in 2020, 2 in 2021). Unlike the full table, this subset is not exactly balanced, so the baseline above does not apply to it. Accuracy / F1:
78	
79	| Classifier | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 |
80	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
81	| logreg | 0.9609 / 0.9392 | 0.9467 / 0.9430 | 0.5304 / 0.6751 | 0.4971 / 0.6596 | 0.5120 / 0.6701 |
82	| random_forest | 0.9683 / 0.9510 | 0.9526 / 0.9496 | 0.5420 / 0.6831 | 0.5049 / 0.6642 | 0.5100 / 0.6698 |
83	| sgd | 0.9644 / 0.9452 | 0.9448 / 0.9419 | 0.5267 / 0.6742 | 0.4957 / 0.6599 | 0.5060 / 0.6692 |
84	
85	The 2017 filter changes F1 by -0.012 (logreg), -0.007 (random forest) and +0.041 (SGD) and raises accuracy for all three (so the duplicates do not explain the good 2017 result), and 2019-2021 barely change because almost no rows are removed. The cliff at 2019 is present in this subset as well. I did not compute a baseline per subset for this table; the 2017 and 2018 subsets are no longer balanced, so precision and accuracy there are not comparable to the full-year numbers.
86	
87	## Caveats
88	
89	- **Noisier late years.** 2019-2021 have 3,000 rows each (1,500 per class) against 18,000 for 2017 and 2018. A rough binomial standard error for accuracy near 0.5 with n = 3,000 is about 0.009 (about 0.0016 for accuracy near 0.95 with n = 18,000), ignoring that duplicate rows (Step 1) make the effective sample smaller. So differences of a few points between 2019, 2020 and 2021 (for example logreg 0.5377 vs 0.5063) are only a few standard errors and I do not rank those years. The three classifiers are evaluated on the same rows, so their differences within a year are paired, but the same limit applies. The step between 2018 and 2019 (about 0.4 in accuracy) is far outside this noise.
90	- **Class balance and precision.** Every test year is exactly 50/50, so precision is comparable across years and the baseline accuracy is the same (0.5000). If the real-world malware share were lower, the same false-positive rate would give lower precision; that is not tested here. The no-duplicate subset is the only one with a changed mix (see above).
91	- **Single fit, no tuning.** The classifiers use the Step 4 default settings and a single `random_state=42` fit, so differences of about one point between classifiers (for example 2017-2018 logreg vs random forest) are small and the run-to-run spread was not measured.
92	- **Pooled numbers.** The pooled Step 5 table is 80% 2017-2018, so it hides the 2019-2021 collapse. The per-year table here is the primary view.
93	- **Duplicates and conflicting labels** (Step 1) are kept, as planned. The KS numbers quoted from Step 2 are effect sizes from a balanced 3,000-row sample per year and were not used to choose anything in Step 6.

"""Step 3: year split, log1p, feature filters and scaling (fit on training years only)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Iterable

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

from src.config import (
    LABEL_COL,
    MIN_SUPPORT,
    TEST_YEARS,
    TRAIN_YEARS,
    TUNE_TRAIN_YEARS,
    TUNE_VAL_YEAR,
    YEAR_COL,
    Z_CLIP,
)
from src.data import feature_columns


def check_no_overlap(train_years: Iterable[int], test_years: Iterable[int]) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError unless train and test years are non-empty, disjoint, and every train year precedes every test year."""
    train, test = set(train_years), set(test_years)
    if not train or not test:
        raise ValueError("train_years and test_years must both be non-empty")
    if train & test:
        raise ValueError(f"train and test years overlap: {sorted(train & test)}")
    if max(train) >= min(test):
        raise ValueError(f"training years {sorted(train)} must all precede test years {sorted(test)}")


def split_by_year(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    train_years: Iterable[int] = TRAIN_YEARS,
    test_years: Iterable[int] = TEST_YEARS,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Return (train, test) frames selected by the `year` column, after checking the years cannot leak."""
    train_years, test_years = tuple(train_years), tuple(test_years)
    check_no_overlap(train_years, test_years)  # guard first: nothing is selected for a bad split
    train = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(train_years)]
    test = df[df[YEAR_COL].isin(test_years)]
    # Every requested year must be present, otherwise the split is silently smaller than asked for.
    for name, part, years in (("train", train, train_years), ("test", test, test_years)):
        missing = sorted(set(years) - set(part[YEAR_COL].unique()))
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"requested {name} years missing from the data: {missing}")
    return train, test


def apply_log1p(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return log(1 + X) as float32; raises ValueError on NaN/inf or negative input (counts must be finite and >= 0)."""
    if not np.isfinite(X).all():  # checked once here, so fit and transform each pay for it once per call
        raise ValueError("log1p input must be finite (no NaN or inf)")
    if X.size and X.min() < 0:
        raise ValueError("log1p input must be non-negative")
    return np.log1p(X, dtype=np.float32)


def nonzero_feature_mask(X_train: np.ndarray, min_support: int = MIN_SUPPORT) -> np.ndarray:
    """Boolean mask of columns with at least `min_support` non-zero values in the TRAINING rows."""
    if min_support < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"min_support must be >= 1, got {min_support}")
    return (X_train != 0).sum(axis=0) >= min_support


class Preprocessor:
    """log1p -> minimum-support column filter -> StandardScaler -> fixed clip, all learned from training rows only.

    sklearn-like (fit/transform/fit_transform), not a BaseEstimator: no get_params, not usable in a Pipeline.
    """

    def __init__(self, min_support: int = MIN_SUPPORT) -> None:
        """Store the support threshold; nothing is learned until `fit`."""
        if min_support < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"min_support must be >= 1, got {min_support}")
        self.min_support = min_support
        self.scaler: StandardScaler | None = None
        self.mask_: np.ndarray | None = None
        self.feature_names_in_: list[str] | None = None
        self.kept_features_: list[str] | None = None
        self.n_all_zero_: int = 0

    def fit(self, X_train_raw: np.ndarray, feature_names: list[str] | None = None) -> "Preprocessor":
        """Learn the column mask and the scaler from raw training counts."""
        X = apply_log1p(X_train_raw)  # log1p keeps zeros at zero, so the mask is the same on raw or logged data
        self.mask_ = nonzero_feature_mask(X, self.min_support)
        self.n_all_zero_ = int((~(X != 0).any(axis=0)).sum())
        names = feature_names if feature_names is not None else [str(i) for i in range(X.shape[1])]
        if len(names) != X.shape[1]:
            raise ValueError(f"got {len(names)} feature names for {X.shape[1]} columns")
        self.feature_names_in_ = list(names)
        self.kept_features_ = [n for n, keep in zip(names, self.mask_) if keep]
        self.scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X[:, self.mask_])
        return self

    def transform(self, X_raw: np.ndarray, clip: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
        """Apply the fitted log1p, mask and scaler (never refits), clip to +-Z_CLIP; returns float32.

        `clip=False` is only for reporting the size of the extreme values.
        """
        if self.scaler is None or self.mask_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Preprocessor must be fit before transform")
        if X_raw.shape[1] != len(self.mask_):
            raise ValueError(f"expected {len(self.mask_)} columns (as in fit), got {X_raw.shape[1]}")
        X = apply_log1p(X_raw)[:, self.mask_]
        Z = self.scaler.transform(X).astype(np.float32)
        # Fixed constant clip: the same for train and test, nothing learned from any data.
        return np.clip(Z, -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP, out=Z) if clip else Z

    def fit_transform(self, X_train_raw: np.ndarray, feature_names: list[str] | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
        """Fit on the training counts and return them transformed."""
        return self.fit(X_train_raw, feature_names).transform(X_train_raw)


def _split_arrays(train: pd.DataFrame, test: pd.DataFrame, features: list[str]) -> dict:
    """Pull raw feature matrices, labels and years out of the train/test frames."""
    return {
        "X_train_raw": train[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32),
        "y_train": train[LABEL_COL].to_numpy(),
        "years_train": train[YEAR_COL].to_numpy(),
        "X_test_raw": test[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32),
        "y_test": test[LABEL_COL].to_numpy(),
        "years_test": test[YEAR_COL].to_numpy(),
    }


def prepare_split(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    train_years: Iterable[int] = TRAIN_YEARS,

def clip_report(X_train: np.ndarray, X_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Max abs z and number of entries beyond +-Z_CLIP for UNCLIPPED scaled matrices; also the values after clipping."""
    rows = []

    features = feature_columns(df)

    n_total = len(features)

    rows = [

        ("after dropping all-zero training columns", n_nonzero),
        (f"after min support >= {pre.min_support} training rows", n_kept),
        ("dropped for low support (1 to min_support-1 non-zero rows)", n_nonzero - n_kept),
        ("dropped columns that are non-zero somewhere in the test years", int((test_active & ~pre.mask_).sum())),
    ]

"""Steps 5 and 6: evaluate the trained classifiers on the held-out test years (malware = positive class)."""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, confusion_matrix, f1_score, precision_score, recall_score

from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS
from src.data import write_data_summary

METRIC_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = ("accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1")


def compute_metrics(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Accuracy, precision, recall and F1 with malware (label 1) as the positive class."""
    kwargs = {"pos_label": 1, "zero_division": 0}  # zero_division=0: no predicted/actual malware gives 0, not an error
    return {
        "accuracy": float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred)),
        "precision": float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
        "recall": float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
        "f1": float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, **kwargs)),
    }


def confusion_counts(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Confusion matrix as TN, FP, FN, TP counts (labels fixed to [0, 1] so a missing class still gives 2x2)."""
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    return {"tn": int(tn), "fp": int(fp), "fn": int(fn), "tp": int(tp)}


def assert_test_years_only(years: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError if any year is outside TEST_YEARS (metrics must never be computed on training years)."""
    bad = sorted(set(np.unique(years).tolist()) - set(TEST_YEARS))
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"evaluation data contains years outside {TEST_YEARS}: {bad}")


def _check_same_length(X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError if X_test and y_test have different numbers of rows."""
    if len(X_test) != len(y_test):
        raise ValueError(f"X_test has {len(X_test)} rows but y_test has {len(y_test)}")


def evaluate_model(model: Any, X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Predict with a fitted model and return its four metrics."""
    return compute_metrics(y_test, model.predict(X_test))


def pooled_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per classifier: model, accuracy, precision, recall, f1, n_test (pooled over the test years)."""
    _check_same_length(X_test, y_test)
    rows = [{"model": name, **evaluate_model(m, X_test, y_test), "n_test": len(y_test)} for name, m in models.items()]
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", *METRIC_NAMES, "n_test"])


def per_year_table(
    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per (model, test year): metrics plus year and n."""
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    rows = []
    for name, m in models.items():
        pred = m.predict(X_test)  # predict once, slice per year
        for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
            sel = years_test == year
            rows.append({"model": name, "year": int(year), **compute_metrics(y_test[sel], pred[sel]), "n": int(sel.sum())})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["model", "year", *METRIC_NAMES, "n"])


def drift_summary(per_year: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per model: F1 in the first and last test year, the drop between them, and the least-squares F1 slope per year."""
    rows = []
    for name, g in per_year.groupby("model", sort=False):
        g = g.sort_values("year")
        first, last = float(g["f1"].iloc[0]), float(g["f1"].iloc[-1])
        slope = float(np.polyfit(g["year"].to_numpy(dtype=float), g["f1"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 1)[0]) if len(g) > 1 else 0.0
        rows.append({"model": name, "first_year": int(g["year"].iloc[0]), "last_year": int(g["year"].iloc[-1]),
                     "f1_first": first, "f1_last": last, "f1_drop": first - last, "f1_slope_per_year": slope})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def year_baseline_table(y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per test year: n, malware/benign counts, malware share and majority-class (baseline) accuracy."""
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    rows = []
    for year in sorted(set(years_test.tolist())):
        y = y_test[years_test == year]
        rows.append({"year": int(year), "n": len(y), "n_malware": int((y == 1).sum()), "n_benign": int((y == 0).sum()),
                     "malware_share": float(np.mean(y == 1)), "baseline_accuracy": baseline_accuracy(y)})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def by_year_export(per_year: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Step 6 file layout: columns classifier, year, n, accuracy, precision, recall, f1."""
    out = per_year.rename(columns={"model": "classifier"})
    return out[["classifier", "year", "n", *METRIC_NAMES]]


def plot_by_year(per_year: pd.DataFrame, path: Path) -> None:
    """Save a two-panel figure (F1 and accuracy by test year, one line per classifier) to path."""
    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")  # no display needed
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4), sharex=True)
    for ax, metric in zip(axes, ("f1", "accuracy")):
        for name, g in per_year.groupby("model", sort=False):
            g = g.sort_values("year")
            ax.plot(g["year"], g[metric], marker="o", label=name)
        ax.set_title(f"{metric.upper() if metric == 'f1' else metric.capitalize()} by test year")
        ax.set_xlabel("test year")
        ax.set_xticks(sorted(per_year["year"].unique()))
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    axes[0].set_ylabel("score (malware = positive class)")
    axes[0].legend()
    fig.tight_layout()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=120)
    plt.close(fig)


def confusion_table(models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per classifier with pooled tn, fp, fn, tp counts."""
    _check_same_length(X_test, y_test)
    return pd.DataFrame([{"model": n, **confusion_counts(y_test, m.predict(X_test))} for n, m in models.items()])


def baseline_accuracy(y_test: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Accuracy of always predicting the majority class of y_test."""
    return float(max(np.mean(y_test == 1), np.mean(y_test == 0)))


def sensitivity_tables(
    models: dict[str, Any], X_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray, years_test: np.ndarray, dup_mask: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Pooled and per-year tables on test rows with NO exact duplicate in the training years (dup_mask False).

    Each table gets an n_excluded column (rows removed by the filter; per year for the per-year table).
    The pooled table also gets n_malware/n_benign (kept) and n_excluded_malware/n_excluded_benign, so the
    change in class mix caused by the filter is visible.
    """
    dup_mask = np.asarray(dup_mask, dtype=bool)
    if len(dup_mask) != len(y_test):
        raise ValueError(f"dup_mask has {len(dup_mask)} entries but there are {len(y_test)} test rows")
    keep = ~dup_mask
    if keep.sum() == 0:
        raise ValueError("every test row has an exact duplicate in the training years; nothing left to evaluate")
    pooled = pooled_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep])
    pooled["n_excluded"] = int(dup_mask.sum())
    # Class counts kept and removed (label 1 = malware, 0 = benign).
    pooled["n_malware"] = int((y_test[keep] == 1).sum())
    pooled["n_benign"] = int((y_test[keep] == 0).sum())
    pooled["n_excluded_malware"] = int((y_test[dup_mask] == 1).sum())
    pooled["n_excluded_benign"] = int((y_test[dup_mask] == 0).sum())
    per_year = per_year_table(models, X_test[keep], y_test[keep], years_test[keep])
    excluded = pd.Series(years_test[dup_mask]).value_counts()
    per_year["n_excluded"] = per_year["year"].map(lambda y: int(excluded.get(y, 0)))
    return pooled, per_year


def save_table(df: pd.DataFrame, stem: str) -> None:
    """Write results/<stem>.csv and results/<stem>.md (floats rounded to 4 decimals in both)."""
    write_data_summary(df.round(4), RESULTS_DIR / stem)

"""Entry point: python -m src.main [--step N]."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys

import pandas as pd

from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS, TRAIN_YEARS
from src.evaluate import (
    assert_test_years_only,
    baseline_accuracy,
    by_year_export,
    confusion_table,
    drift_summary,
    per_year_table,
    plot_by_year,
    pooled_table,
    save_table,
    sensitivity_tables,
    year_baseline_table,
)
from src.models import save_models, train_all_from_split, train_with_report
from src.preprocess import filter_report, prepare_split, split_table
from src.drift import run_drift_analysis
from src.data import (
    _row_hashes,
    train_duplicate_mask,
    feature_columns,
    file_table,
    label_conflict_mask,
    load_all,
    summarize_data,
    write_data_summary,
)


def run_step1() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Step 1: load and combine the data, write results/step1_*.csv|md, print a summary."""
    df = load_all()
    summary = summarize_data(df)
    write_data_summary(summary, RESULTS_DIR / "step1_data_summary")
    write_data_summary(file_table(df), RESULTS_DIR / "step1_file_table")
    n_features = len(feature_columns(df))
    print(f"Step 1: {len(df)} rows, {n_features} feature columns, memory {df.memory_usage().sum() / 1e6:.0f} MB")
    print(summary.to_string(index=False))
    # Feature vectors that occur with both labels anywhere in the data (all years pooled).
    hashes = _row_hashes(df)
    conflict = label_conflict_mask(hashes, df["label"].to_numpy())
    print(f"Label conflicts (all years pooled): {len(set(hashes[conflict]))} vectors, {int(conflict.sum())} rows")
    return df


def run_step2(df: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 2: KS feature drift and the concept-drift accuracy matrix; writes results/step2_*."""
    tables = run_drift_analysis(load_all() if df is None else df)
    for name in ("ks_vs_2014", "ks_consecutive", "accuracy_matrix"):
        print(f"Step 2 {name}:")
        print(tables[name].round(4).to_string())
    return tables


def run_step3(df: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """Step 3: preprocess (fit on 2014-2016 only); writes results/step3_*."""
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS)
    pre = split["preprocessor"]
    counts = filter_report(df, pre, TEST_YEARS)
    table = split_table(split)
    write_data_summary(counts, RESULTS_DIR / "step3_feature_counts")
    write_data_summary(table, RESULTS_DIR / "step3_split")
    write_data_summary(split["clip_stats"], RESULTS_DIR / "step3_clip")
    pd.Series(pre.kept_features_, name="feature").to_csv(RESULTS_DIR / "step3_kept_features.csv", index=False)
    print(f"Step 3: X_train {split['X_train'].shape} {split['X_train'].dtype}, X_test {split['X_test'].shape}")
    print(split["clip_stats"].to_string(index=False))
    print(counts.to_string(index=False))
    print(table.to_string(index=False))
    return split


def run_step4(split: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 4: train the three classifiers on 2014-2016; prints TRAINING-only sanity numbers.

    Returns (models, report) so Step 5 can reuse the fitted models instead of retraining.
    """
    split = prepare_split(load_all(), TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    models, report = train_with_report(split)
    save_models(models)
    write_data_summary(report, RESULTS_DIR / "step4_training")
    print("Step 4 (training-set sanity check only, NOT evaluation):")
    print(report.to_string(index=False))
    return models, report


def run_step5(
    df: pd.DataFrame | None = None, split: dict | None = None, models: dict | None = None
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 5: evaluate the three classifiers on the pooled test years 2017-2021; writes results/step5_*.

    models: fitted Step 4 classifiers to reuse; trained on 2014-2016 here only when None (e.g. --step 5 alone).
    """
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    if models is None:
        models = train_all_from_split(split)  # fit on 2014-2016 only
    X_test, y_test, years_test = split["X_test"], split["y_test"], split["years_test"]
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    main_table = pooled_table(models, X_test, y_test)
    base = baseline_accuracy(y_test)
    main_table["baseline_accuracy"] = base  # majority-class reference for the accuracy column
    # Mask over all rows of df; select the test rows (split_by_year keeps df order).
    dup_mask = train_duplicate_mask(df)[df["year"].isin(TEST_YEARS).to_numpy()]
    no_dup, _ = sensitivity_tables(models, X_test, y_test, years_test, dup_mask)
    confusion = confusion_table(models, X_test, y_test)
    save_table(main_table, "step5_metrics")
    save_table(no_dup, "step5_pooled_no_dup")
    save_table(confusion, "step5_confusion")
    print(f"Step 5 (pooled test years, n={len(y_test)}; majority-class accuracy {base:.4f}):")
    print(main_table.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    base_nd = baseline_accuracy(y_test[~dup_mask])
    print(f"Sensitivity (no exact training duplicate; {int(dup_mask.sum())} test rows excluded; "
          f"majority-class accuracy of subset {base_nd:.4f}):")
    print(no_dup.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(confusion.to_string(index=False))
    return {"metrics": main_table, "no_dup": no_dup, "confusion": confusion}


def run_step6(
    df: pd.DataFrame | None = None, split: dict | None = None, models: dict | None = None
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 6: per-year evaluation of the three classifiers on 2017-2021; writes results/step6_*.

    models: fitted Step 4 classifiers to reuse; trained on 2014-2016 here only when None (e.g. --step 6 alone).
    Nothing is refit on a test year.
    """
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    if models is None:
        models = train_all_from_split(split)  # fit on 2014-2016 only
    X_test, y_test, years_test = split["X_test"], split["y_test"], split["years_test"]
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    per_year = per_year_table(models, X_test, y_test, years_test)
    baseline = year_baseline_table(y_test, years_test)
    drift = drift_summary(per_year)
    # Sensitivity: only test rows with no exact duplicate in 2014-2016 (mask is over all rows of df).
    dup_mask = train_duplicate_mask(df)[df["year"].isin(TEST_YEARS).to_numpy()]
    _, per_year_nd = sensitivity_tables(models, X_test, y_test, years_test, dup_mask)
    save_table(by_year_export(per_year), "step6_by_year")
    save_table(baseline, "step6_baseline_by_year")
    save_table(drift, "step6_drift_summary")
    save_table(per_year_nd.rename(columns={"model": "classifier"}), "step6_per_year_no_dup")
    plot_by_year(per_year, RESULTS_DIR / "step6_by_year.png")
    print("Step 6 (per test year; malware = positive class):")
    print(by_year_export(per_year).round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(baseline.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(drift.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    return {"by_year": per_year, "baseline": baseline, "drift": drift, "no_dup": per_year_nd}


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the pipeline (Steps 1-6 exist so far); --step N runs one step."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Project 2 pipeline")
    parser.add_argument("--step", type=int, choices=range(1, 8), help="run a single step (1-7)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.step not in (None, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6):
        print(f"Step {args.step} is not implemented yet.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1  # non-zero so callers can tell nothing ran
    df = run_step1()
    if args.step in (None, 2):
        run_step2(df)
    split = None
    if args.step in (None, 3):
        split = run_step3(df)
    models = None
    if args.step in (None, 4):
        models, _ = run_step4(split)
    if args.step in (None, 5):
        run_step5(df, split, models)
    if args.step in (None, 6):

"""Entry point: python -m src.main [--step N]."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys

import pandas as pd

from src.config import RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS, TRAIN_YEARS
from src.evaluate import (
    assert_test_years_only,
    baseline_accuracy,
    by_year_export,
    confusion_table,
    drift_summary,
    per_year_table,
    plot_by_year,
    pooled_table,
    save_table,
    sensitivity_tables,
    year_baseline_table,
)
from src.models import save_models, train_all_from_split, train_with_report
from src.preprocess import filter_report, prepare_split, split_table
from src.drift import run_drift_analysis
from src.data import (
    _row_hashes,
    train_duplicate_mask,
    feature_columns,
    file_table,
    label_conflict_mask,
    load_all,
    summarize_data,
    write_data_summary,
)


def run_step1() -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Step 1: load and combine the data, write results/step1_*.csv|md, print a summary."""
    df = load_all()
    summary = summarize_data(df)
    write_data_summary(summary, RESULTS_DIR / "step1_data_summary")
    write_data_summary(file_table(df), RESULTS_DIR / "step1_file_table")
    n_features = len(feature_columns(df))
    print(f"Step 1: {len(df)} rows, {n_features} feature columns, memory {df.memory_usage().sum() / 1e6:.0f} MB")
    print(summary.to_string(index=False))
    # Feature vectors that occur with both labels anywhere in the data (all years pooled).
    hashes = _row_hashes(df)
    conflict = label_conflict_mask(hashes, df["label"].to_numpy())
    print(f"Label conflicts (all years pooled): {len(set(hashes[conflict]))} vectors, {int(conflict.sum())} rows")
    return df


def run_step2(df: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 2: KS feature drift and the concept-drift accuracy matrix; writes results/step2_*."""
    tables = run_drift_analysis(load_all() if df is None else df)
    for name in ("ks_vs_2014", "ks_consecutive", "accuracy_matrix"):
        print(f"Step 2 {name}:")
        print(tables[name].round(4).to_string())
    return tables


def run_step3(df: pd.DataFrame | None = None) -> dict:
    """Step 3: preprocess (fit on 2014-2016 only); writes results/step3_*."""
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS)
    pre = split["preprocessor"]
    counts = filter_report(df, pre, TEST_YEARS)
    table = split_table(split)
    write_data_summary(counts, RESULTS_DIR / "step3_feature_counts")
    write_data_summary(table, RESULTS_DIR / "step3_split")
    write_data_summary(split["clip_stats"], RESULTS_DIR / "step3_clip")
    pd.Series(pre.kept_features_, name="feature").to_csv(RESULTS_DIR / "step3_kept_features.csv", index=False)
    print(f"Step 3: X_train {split['X_train'].shape} {split['X_train'].dtype}, X_test {split['X_test'].shape}")
    print(split["clip_stats"].to_string(index=False))
    print(counts.to_string(index=False))
    print(table.to_string(index=False))
    return split


def run_step4(split: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 4: train the three classifiers on 2014-2016; prints TRAINING-only sanity numbers.

    Returns (models, report) so Step 5 can reuse the fitted models instead of retraining.
    """
    split = prepare_split(load_all(), TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    models, report = train_with_report(split)
    save_models(models)
    write_data_summary(report, RESULTS_DIR / "step4_training")
    print("Step 4 (training-set sanity check only, NOT evaluation):")
    print(report.to_string(index=False))
    return models, report


def run_step5(
    df: pd.DataFrame | None = None, split: dict | None = None, models: dict | None = None
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 5: evaluate the three classifiers on the pooled test years 2017-2021; writes results/step5_*.

    models: fitted Step 4 classifiers to reuse; trained on 2014-2016 here only when None (e.g. --step 5 alone).
    """
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    if models is None:
        models = train_all_from_split(split)  # fit on 2014-2016 only
    X_test, y_test, years_test = split["X_test"], split["y_test"], split["years_test"]
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    main_table = pooled_table(models, X_test, y_test)
    base = baseline_accuracy(y_test)
    main_table["baseline_accuracy"] = base  # majority-class reference for the accuracy column
    # Mask over all rows of df; select the test rows (split_by_year keeps df order).
    dup_mask = train_duplicate_mask(df)[df["year"].isin(TEST_YEARS).to_numpy()]
    no_dup, _ = sensitivity_tables(models, X_test, y_test, years_test, dup_mask)
    confusion = confusion_table(models, X_test, y_test)
    save_table(main_table, "step5_metrics")
    save_table(no_dup, "step5_pooled_no_dup")
    save_table(confusion, "step5_confusion")
    print(f"Step 5 (pooled test years, n={len(y_test)}; majority-class accuracy {base:.4f}):")
    print(main_table.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    base_nd = baseline_accuracy(y_test[~dup_mask])
    print(f"Sensitivity (no exact training duplicate; {int(dup_mask.sum())} test rows excluded; "
          f"majority-class accuracy of subset {base_nd:.4f}):")
    print(no_dup.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(confusion.to_string(index=False))
    return {"metrics": main_table, "no_dup": no_dup, "confusion": confusion}


def run_step6(
    df: pd.DataFrame | None = None, split: dict | None = None, models: dict | None = None
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Step 6: per-year evaluation of the three classifiers on 2017-2021; writes results/step6_*.

    models: fitted Step 4 classifiers to reuse; trained on 2014-2016 here only when None (e.g. --step 6 alone).
    Nothing is refit on a test year.
    """
    df = load_all() if df is None else df
    split = prepare_split(df, TRAIN_YEARS, TEST_YEARS) if split is None else split
    if models is None:
        models = train_all_from_split(split)  # fit on 2014-2016 only
    X_test, y_test, years_test = split["X_test"], split["y_test"], split["years_test"]
    assert_test_years_only(years_test)
    per_year = per_year_table(models, X_test, y_test, years_test)
    baseline = year_baseline_table(y_test, years_test)
    drift = drift_summary(per_year)
    # Sensitivity: only test rows with no exact duplicate in 2014-2016 (mask is over all rows of df).
    dup_mask = train_duplicate_mask(df)[df["year"].isin(TEST_YEARS).to_numpy()]
    _, per_year_nd = sensitivity_tables(models, X_test, y_test, years_test, dup_mask)
    save_table(by_year_export(per_year), "step6_by_year")
    save_table(baseline, "step6_baseline_by_year")
    save_table(drift, "step6_drift_summary")
    conf_year = confusion_by_year(models, X_test, y_test, years_test)
    save_table(per_year_nd.rename(columns={"model": "classifier"}), "step6_per_year_no_dup")
    save_table(conf_year, "step6_confusion_by_year")
    plot_by_year(per_year, RESULTS_DIR / "step6_by_year.png")
    print("Step 6 (per test year; malware = positive class):")
    print(by_year_export(per_year).round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(baseline.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print(drift.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    print("Confusion counts and predicted-malware share by year:")
    print(conf_year.round(4).to_string(index=False))
    out = {"by_year": per_year, "baseline": baseline, "drift": drift, "no_dup": per_year_nd, "confusion_by_year": conf_year}
    if "clip_by_year" in split:  # preprocessing extremes per year (measured before clipping in prepare_split)
        save_table(split["clip_by_year"], "step6_clip_by_year")
        print("Clip share and mean |z| by year (before clipping):")
        print(split["clip_by_year"].round(4).to_string(index=False))
        out["clip_by_year"] = split["clip_by_year"]
    return out


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the pipeline (Steps 1-6 exist so far); --step N runs one step."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Project 2 pipeline")
    parser.add_argument("--step", type=int, choices=range(1, 8), help="run a single step (1-7)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.step not in (None, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6):
        print(f"Step {args.step} is not implemented yet.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1  # non-zero so callers can tell nothing ran
    df = run_step1()
    if args.step in (None, 2):
        run_step2(df)
    split = None
    if args.step in (None, 3):
        split = run_step3(df)
    models = None
    if args.step in (None, 4):
        models, _ = run_step4(split)
    if args.step in (None, 5):
        run_step5(df, split, models)
    if args.step in (None, 6):
        run_step6(df, split, models)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
